newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh drivers riot after fuel price rise.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh drivers riot after fuel price rise.

text.p: Bangladeshi drivers and minicab owners went on the rampage on Tuesday, damaging more than 100 vehicles after the government raised the price of petroleum products by up to 57 percent, police and witnesses said.
An official announcement said the price rise, with immediate effect, was agreed at a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday.
It said: "The prices of petroleum products have been refixed considering the devaluation of the Bangladesh taka against the U.S. dollar as well as (prices on the) international market."
The prices of unleaded petrol per litre rose to 23 taka from 14.65, leaded petrol 21 taka from 13.7 and diesel 12.95 from 12.7.
The central bank on Monday readjusted the taka down more than one percent to 44.45/65 against the U.S. dollar from 44.00/20.
The central bank made a similar adjustment to the currency in July.
Witnesses said owners and drivers of three-wheeled minicabs rampaged on the streets of Chittagong, throwing stones and drink bottles at other vehicles.
They damaged more than 100 buses and cars, police told reporters.
Police in the port city used batons to disperse transport workers armed with sticks and stones, and said they arrested at least 50 people.
Police said no injuries had been reported. Witnesses said about a dozen people suffered minor injuries.
Witnesses said most vehicles, except for trucks, had withdrawn from Chittagong streets by Monday noon.
Truck drivers remained calm because of the small price rise for diesel, the witnesses said.
The situation in the capital Dhaka was also tense, with cab operators holding rallies and protest marches. They warned of unspecified tough action unless the fuel prices were lowered.
Hundreds of cars queued up at filling stations in the capital to fill their tanks, fearing the protesters might force a temporary suspension in fuel supplies.
"Everybody is panicked today. It (fuel price rise) may have a chain reaction, including higher transport fares and soaring prices of essentials," one official said.
